name: MALAYSIA
tagline: All of Asia in one place
lead: Malaysia is in Southeast Asia. One part hangs down from Thailand. Two big states lie on the island of Borneo. Its rainforests are older than the Amazon. Many peoples share its busy streets and great food.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: KL — a great SE Asian skyline

geo: Rainforest covers the hills of the Malaysian peninsula. The Titiwangsa mountains run down it like a green backbone.
The two states, Sabah and Sarawak, lie on Borneo. Rivers work as roads there. Mount Kinabalu rises above the clouds.
animals: Malaysia's rainforest is over 130 million years old. Orangutans swing through Borneo's trees. Pygmy elephants wade in Sabah's rivers. Fewer than 150 Malayan tigers remain in the wild.
Proboscis monkeys have huge noses and honk from riverside trees. The Rafflesia, up to a metre wide, is the world's largest flower. Fireflies light up mangrove trees on the Selangor River.
culture: Malay, Chinese, Indian and over 60 native groups live here. Hari Raya, Chinese New Year, Deepavali and Christmas are all public holidays. People often join each other's parties.
Food is the national favourite. Try nasi lemak (coconut rice), roti canai (flatbread) and laksa (noodle soup). All are a short walk apart in any town.
history: Malacca was the top trading port in Southeast Asia in the 1400s. Merchants from Arabia, India, China and Java came. The Portuguese took it in 1511, then the Dutch, then the British.
Britain joined the sultans' kingdoms into British Malaya. Malaysia became independent on 31 August 1957. Everyone shouted Merdeka (freedom)! Malaysia became a union of states in 1963.
wows: The world's biggest cave room, in Mulu National Park, fits 40 Boeing 747s.
Malaysia makes about a quarter of the world's palm oil, one of the top two makers.
A sky bridge links the Petronas Twin Towers at floors 41 and 42, 170 metres up.
The South China Sea splits Malaysia in two.
The tapir, a pig-like forest animal, has barely changed in 20 million years.
Kuala Lumpur means 'muddy river meeting' and began as a tin-mining camp in the 1850s.
Around three million bats spiral out of Deer Cave at dusk.

myths.myth: The world's biggest flower smells sweet
myths.fact: The Rafflesia smells like rotting meat. That draws flies, which carry its pollen.
The Cameron Highlands sit at 1,500 m and are cool enough to grow strawberries and tea year-round.
